title: The Palace of a Thousand Logs
synopsis: A pine tree note: one mark has a new line.
goal: Find out where the palace logs went, and who took them.

notes: Played under the glass (InspectScene): the log whose mark has one pale, new cut is the one the note describes; its torn yard tag leads to the typed word. Take the new line away (the carvers' rule on the yard board, told by Duri: a stronger sound adds one line, ㄴ then ㄷ) and 다 was 나: good logs, for the palace gates.
The marks are words of the app (each spot's line): the logs in the picture have plain carved patches, no letters.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheet of timber_yard.webp (picture.measuredOn): the thick log end on the left, the thin bent log in the centre, the tall straight log on the right with its blank tag hanging just right of it; the game writes each mark on its log's carved patch; no two areas overlap.

learningGoal.title: Reading marks, numbers and a palace's story

objectives: Find the mark with a new line.
intro: Winter, 1866. You are a detective in Hanyang.
The Heungseon Daewongun is the King's father.
Now pine logs fill the yard.
But today, palace logs are missing.
play.caseSummary: At night, Mr. Pyo changed ten palace logs. One new line made 나 into 다: logs to sell. He bought them. Duri wrote the note. He drew a pine tree. Gyeongbokgung burned in 1592. The Heungseon Daewongun rebuilt it, 1865 to 1868. People paid money and did hard work.

notes: PART 10 (2026-11-06), Case 04. The Heungseon Daewongun is real; his words here are made up. Duri, Mr. Pyo, the clerk, the yard board, the marks and the missing logs are made up.

Ends on checked facts: the final talk's cost question closes on the real cost of the rebuilding (h4 forced gifts of money, h5 the new coin of 1866 and rising prices, h6 farmers called to work), and the ending states the real rebuilding (h2 begun in the fourth month of 1865, the Daewongun leading it; h3 finished in 1868, the King moved in).

PART 2 (2026-11-09): stands alone. The stroke rule is taught in this case (Duri and the yard board); M2 counts twelve and six, then two and sixteen; M3 follows the traces to Mr. Pyo's cart (trace_deduction, measured on palace_site.webp); the final's three presents each take one card of this case (three cards, lit from the third miss).
